# Why Nearly Half of eDiscovery Matters Now Need Private Deployment

It’s Thursday afternoon, and after a quiet week a big matter lands on your desk. The data you need is scattered across a dozen collaboration apps. From product brainstorming boards in [Miro](https://www.onna.com/connectors/miro) to communication records in [Slack](https://www.onna.com/connectors/slack), relevant data is everywhere. The volume dwarfs your last case, and the client contract says certain data points cannot leave a specific regional jurisdiction.

There’s one decision upfront that determines the course of the entire case. Where will this matter run? By that, we mean: will it run on privately deployed or on-premises software, or in the cloud?

In the [2026 eDiscovery Buyers Report: AI and Deployment Trends](https://www.revealdata.com/guides/2026-ediscovery-buyers-report), private and on-premises deployment showed up as an increasingly popular choice for legal technology deployment.

## What Is Privately Deployed eDiscovery?

[Private deployment](https://www.revealdata.com/rpd) is when your eDiscovery review platform runs on infrastructure that stays single-tenant and under your control. The eDiscovery Buyers Report sorted deployment into three types.

1. **Public cloud** is multi-tenant software, hosted and operated by the vendor on shared infrastructure.
2. **Private cloud** is a single-tenant environment dedicated to your organization, hosted by the vendor or inside your own cloud account.
3. **On premises** is infrastructure your organization owns and runs in its own data center.

"Private deployment" refers to the second and third together, because both keep your environment single-tenant and under your control. Run more than one of these at the same time and you have a hybrid model. In a hybrid model, each matter goes to the environment that best fits its cost, regulatory, and infrastructure needs.

## Why Is the Share of Privately Deployed Matters Climbing?

On average, [46% of matters](https://www.revealdata.com/guides/2026-ediscovery-buyers-report) already require private or on-premises deployment today. That’s nearly half the work, and that number is only rising. [91% of buyers](https://www.revealdata.com/guides/2026-ediscovery-buyers-report) say the share of matters requiring private deployment has risen over the past 24 months, with 29% describing the increase as significant.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65c4ab17d1f4702114123723/6a988be86d714350da9a4eb2_Screenshot%202026-09-02%20154841.png)

This increase is driven by two factors: **cost and obligation.**

### The Cost of Deployment

eDiscovery costs have grown about [20% a year over the last three years](https://www.revealdata.com/guides/2026-ediscovery-buyers-report), and organizations report that their data doubles on average every 21 months. The mass adoption of AI tools promises to steepen that curve, since every AI-assisted chat, transcript, and generated draft becomes potentially discoverable material. Under consumption-based models tied to data volume, that growth converts directly into spend. And so many teams would rather run heavy workloads on infrastructure they control, where costs aren’t tied as tightly to volume.

### Regulatory and Data Obligations

The second driver is obligation. 77.5% of buyers rate regulatory or data sovereignty requirements as an important factor in deployment choice. These obligations tend to be matter-specific and rarely negotiable. When a regulation like the European GDPR or a client mandate dictates where data must sit, cloud preference does not override it. You need a deployment option that can meet the requirement, not a single destination that hopes the requirement never comes up.

With those obligations in mind, you can see why buyers are skeptical of a one-size-fits-all answer. Looking forward, hybrid approaches are growing in popularity: 48% of survey participants expect to run a hybrid approach within 24 months, either retaining their current mix or moving to a mix of models, and no single deployment model commands a majority.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65c4ab17d1f4702114123723/6a988bf43feabcdae595789a_Screenshot%202026-09-02%20154848.png)

The goal is not to pick the one right place for every matter. The goal is to be able to place each matter where it belongs.

## Determining If Private or Hybrid Deployment Is Right for You

You do not need to rebuild everything at once. You need a plan that treats deployment as a variable you control, matter by matter. Here is a practical path.

1. **Map your matters to their real requirements.** For each recurring matter type, write down what actually governs it: data residency rules, client contractual mandates, sensitivity of the data, and expected volume. This turns a vague "we might need private someday" into a concrete list of what runs where.
2. **Assume your data volume will grow.** Plan capacity against the reality that data doubles roughly every 21 months and AI adoption accelerates it. Infrastructure you own and control gives you a cost curve you can predict rather than one that floats with a vendor meter.
3. **Choose infrastructure you can control.** Look for a platform that runs in private cloud or on premises, on hardware and cloud accounts you govern, so sensitive matters never share tenancy with anyone else.
4. **Keep portability front of mind.** Favor an architecture that lets you move a matter between deployment models without re-tooling or renegotiating your platform every time. Flexibility you cannot exercise is not flexibility.
5. **Pressure-test the recommendation.** When a vendor steers you toward one deployment model, ask whose interest it serves. 68% of buyers believe deployment recommendations serve vendors’ commercial interests over their own needs. That skepticism is healthy. Make the vendor show their work.

Nearly half of your matters may already belong somewhere other than the public cloud, and that share is rising, which makes deployment flexibility a decision worth making on purpose. ## Common Questions

### What is the difference between private cloud and on-premises eDiscovery?

Private cloud is a single-tenant environment dedicated to your organization, hosted either by the vendor or inside your own cloud account. On premises is infrastructure your organization owns and operates in its own data center. Both keep the environment under your control and are often grouped together under the umbrella term "private deployment."

### Is private deployment only for highly regulated industries?

No. Regulation and data sovereignty are major drivers, and 77.5% of buyers rate them as important decision-making factors when it comes to deployment. But cost predictability, security posture, and control over AI data are pushing a much broader set of organizations toward private and hybrid models. On average, 46% of all matters now require private deployment.

### Does moving to private deployment mean giving up modern AI?

It should not. The concern that private deployment means older or weaker tools is out of date. Platforms built for this reality run the same AI and analytics privately that they run in the cloud, so you can keep advanced capabilities on infrastructure you control.

### What is a hybrid deployment model?

A hybrid model runs more than one deployment type at once, sending each matter to the environment that best fits its cost, security, residency, and AI requirements. 48% of buyers expect to run a hybrid approach within 24 months.

### Why are eDiscovery costs rising so fast?

Data volume is the main driver. Organizations report their data doubles on average every 21 months, and eDiscovery costs have grown about 20% a year over three years. AI adoption adds fuel, since AI-generated content becomes discoverable and increases the volume that must be processed and reviewed.
